_comment: Wall-clock budgets in seconds per `test:*` suite, checked by
scripts/check-suite-budgets.mjs at the end of `pnpm test`.
Raise a number only with a recorded measurement in the commit
message — this file is the ratchet that keeps a twenty-minute suite
from growing back one reasonable-looking test at a time. AGENTS.md
has the cheaper places to put a new assertion.
`suites` and `totalSeconds` are the only numbers that govern. The
`_measured…` blocks are recorded history, and each one is named
`_measured<YYYY_MM_DD>[_<qualifier>]@<branch>` — the branch it was
measured on, verbatim after the `@`. The check compares a run only
against a block labelled with the branch you are on and refuses the
rest: run 3's babysitter compared a feature-branch measurement
against main's and raised a budget for a slowdown that was not there,
and the labels were already there — nobody read them. When you record
a new block, label it, and append it (the check treats the last
matching block as the newest).
Budgets are ~30% above the slowest observed IN-CHAIN run, not above
the suite measured alone. The distinction matters and cost round 2 a
red gate: run on its own, qa-orchestration is 35.3 / 35.8 / 35.8s,
but inside `pnpm test` the same suite measured 35.4s and then 51.8s.
A suite measured alone is stable to about 2%; the same suite inside
the chain can land 45% higher. `scripts/timed-suite.mjs` reads the
in-chain number, so that is what a budget has to cover — a gate that
trips on ordinary variance just teaches people to raise it.
NOTE on the 2026-08-26 round-2 drop: most of it came from making
fixture repos ignore the host git configuration (see the comment in
vitest.config.ts). A machine-wide `core.hooksPath` was running a
third-party hook on every fixture commit, checkout and merge. These
budgets therefore assume no such hook runs. On a host that never had
one the numbers were always lower, and the budgets are still met.

883 tests, idle machine. The heavy suites cost ~2x main's numbers

that previously skipped the sanity/base gates now spawn pnpm for

numbers. When this branch merges to main, re-measure; reducing the
per-scenario sanity cost is follow-up work, not a test regression.
Three measurements of this same tree inside AFK run 4's gates,
load rising as agents accumulated: fast 87.5 -> 105.1 -> 130.5s
(gate r1, gate r2, QA r2's own run) against the 84.8s idle
baseline and the 110s budget; orchestrator 329.1 -> 382.4s
against 400. QA r2's 130.5s tripped the fast budget and became a
blocking Major finding on slice #78 with zero failing tests.
During an AFK run the resident agents ARE the environment, and
the budget must cover the in-chain number in that environment:
fast raised 110 -> 170 (~30% above the 130.5 worst), orchestrator
400 -> 500 (~30% above 382.4). Operator raise, not a generator
edit — the ratchet rule reserves this for a recorded measurement.
AFK run 5. Slice #79's generator measured test:heavy:orchestrator at
~516s against the 500s budget with zero failing tests, under its own
load plus a resident babysitter session. Same settled class as run 4:
wall-clock variance under agent load, not a test regression. Raised
500 -> 560 pre-emptively, because the consumer of this number is the
pre-ship gate's test:budgets — which runs with guardian reviews and a
babysitter resident, and where a red gate on a 3% overshoot would
block a ship after three-plus hours of work. #78's own base gate ran
its tests step at 691.9s, under the 820s feature-branch baseline, so
nothing here indicates the suite itself got slower.
